title: 考研英语二 2011 年 · 阅读理解 Part A (Text 1-4)
intro: 共 4 篇文章，每篇 5 道多选题，共 20 题 × 2 分 = 40 分。

passages.title: Text 1 · 公司治理与外部董事
paragraphs: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs's board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University. For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism. But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman's compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked?

By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board. The position was just taking up too much time, she said. Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board.

Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals. If the sky, and the share price is falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises. The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004. Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next.

The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those "surprise" disappearances by directors under the age of 70. They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%. The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse. The effect tended to be larger for larger firms.

Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship. Often they "trade up," leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms. But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred. Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives.
Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.
translations: 2000年1月，露丝·西蒙斯以外部董事的身份加入高盛集团董事会；一年后，她出任布朗大学校长。在此后的十年里，她显然妥善兼顾了这两个职位，并未招致多少批评。然而到2009年底，西蒙斯女士因曾任职于高盛薪酬委员会而受到猛烈抨击：她怎能让那些巨额奖金的发放悄无声息地通过？
到了次年2月，西蒙斯女士辞去了董事会职务。她说这个职位占用了太多时间。在公司董事会中，外部董事理应充当有益且更客观公正的顾问。
由于他们早已在别处积累了财富与声望，按理说他们拥有足够的独立性来对首席执行官的提议提出异议。当天塌地陷、股价暴跌之时，外部董事应当能够凭借自身经历过的危机来提供建言。来自俄亥俄大学的研究人员使用了一个涵盖1989年至2004年间1万多家公司及6.4万多名不同董事的数据库。随后，他们只需核查哪些董事在两期委托书之间依然留任。
离开董事会最可能的原因是年龄，因此研究人员将重点放在70岁以下董事的“意外”离职上。他们发现，在发生意外离职后，公司随后不得不重述收益的概率增加了近20%。被卷入联邦集体诉讼的可能性也有所增加，且股票表现很可能更差。这种效应对于大公司往往更为显著。
尽管外部董事的离职与公司随后的糟糕表现之间存在关联这一现象发人深省，但并不意味着这些董事总是在跳下一艘正在下沉的船。他们往往是“往高处走”，离开风险更大、规模较小的公司，转投更大、更稳定的企业。但研究人员认为，如果外部董事在坏消息曝光之前离开公司，往往更容易免遭声誉受损，哪怕回溯历史表明在发生违规行为时他们仍在董事会任职。想要在困难时期留住外部董事的公司，可能必须建立激励机制。
否则，外部董事将会效仿西蒙斯女士的做法——如今她在大学校园里再度广受欢迎。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Ms. Simmons was criticized for ______.

options.label: D
options.text: leaving the board in tough times

questions.analysis: 第一段末句指出“how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked”，西蒙斯女士因在高盛薪酬委员会任职却听任巨额奖金通过而受到严厉抨击，说明她未尽到监督制衡之责，故选 [B]。

questions.stem: We learn from Paragraph 2 that outside directors are supposed to be ______.
questions.analysis: 第二段最后一句指出外部董事应充当“helpful, yet less biased, advisers”，并在第三段强调其“have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals”，即独立的建言顾问，故选 [D]。

questions.stem: According to the researchers from Ohio University, after an outside director's surprise departure, the firm is likely to ______.

options.label: C
options.text: do less well in the stock market

questions.analysis: 第四段第三句明确指出“and the stock is likely to perform worse”（并且股票很可能会表现更差），与选项 [C]“在股市中表现欠佳”完全契合，故选 [C]。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that outside directors ______.

options.label: A
options.text: may stay for the attractive offers from the firm

options.label: B
options.text: have often had records of wrongdoings in the firm

options.label: C
options.text: are accustomed to stress-free work in the firm

options.label: D
options.text: will decline incentives from the firm

questions.analysis: 第五段末句指出“Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives.”（想在艰难时期留住外部董事的公司可能需要设立激励机制），可反推外部董事可能会因丰厚的条件选择留任，故选 [A]。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the role of outside directors is ______.
questions.analysis: 作者在全文中肯定了外部董事能够提供较少偏见的有益建议以及应对危机的独立性，认为这一角色对公司治理具有建设性价值，态度是积极正向的（positive），故选 [B]。

passages.title: Text 2 · 美国报业生存困境与转型
paragraphs: Whatever happened to the death of newspapers? A year ago the end seemed near. The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet. Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom.

America's Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers. Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them? It will hold another meeting soon.

But the discussions now seem out of date. In much of the world there is little sign of crisis. German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession. Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit.

Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same. It has not been much fun. Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard. The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007.

Readers are paying more for slimmer products. Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs. Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further. Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers.

American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads. Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD). In Japan the proportion is 35%. Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable.

The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive. Car and film reviewers have gone. So have science and general business reporters. Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off.
Newspapers are less complete as a result. But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.
translations: 报纸消亡论究竟怎么样了？一年前，终局似乎近在咫尺。经济衰退威胁要带走那些尚未流失到互联网上的广告和读者。《旧金山纪事报》等报纸甚至在持续记录着自身的覆灭。
美国联邦贸易委员会就如何挽救报业展开了一轮会谈。报纸是否应该转为慈善机构？国家是否应该对它们进行补贴？该委员会不久还将举行另一次会议。
但这些讨论如今看来似乎已经过时了。在世界大部分地区，几乎看不到危机的迹象。德国和巴西的报纸已经摆脱了经济衰退的影响。就连处在全球报业最艰难角落的美国报纸，不仅挺了过来，甚至往往恢复了盈利。
虽然不像几年前那样普遍保持20%的利润率，但终究还是盈利了。这个过程并没有多少乐趣可言。许多报社通过大肆裁减记者来维持运转。美国新闻编辑协会估计，自2007年以来已有13,500个新闻采编岗位消失。
读者正在为内容更薄的报纸支付更高的费用。一些报纸甚至敢于拒绝向偏远郊区配送。然而，这些孤注一掷的举措已被证明是正确的，而且令许多记者感到遗憾的是，这些举措还可以进一步推行。报纸正转变为更具平衡性的商业模式，读者收入与广告收入的结构更为健康合理。
长期以来，美国报纸对广告的依赖非同寻常。经合组织（OECD）数据显示，2008年其总收入的整整87%来自广告。而在日本，这一比例仅为35%。毫不奇怪，日本的报纸要稳定得多。
席卷新闻编辑室的旋风伤害了所有人，但大部分损失主要集中在报纸最缺乏特色的领域。汽车和电影评论员已经离开，科学和通用商业记者也是如此。驻外记者站更是遭到了无情的大幅裁撤。
结果便是报纸的内容不如以往全面。但在如今的报业中，全面性已不再是一项美德。

questions.stem: By saying "Newspapers like…their own doom" (Lines 3-4, Para. 1), the author indicates that newspapers ______.
questions.analysis: 第一段生动描述了衰退夺走读者与广告、报纸甚至在亲自记录自己的灭亡，形象地说明报纸当时已陷入生死攸关的绝境（in a desperate situation），故选 [D]。

questions.stem: Some newspapers refused delivery to distant suburbs probably because ______.

options.label: C
options.text: journalists reported little about these areas

questions.analysis: 第五段第二句提到报社拒绝向远郊送报，紧随其后指出这些绝望之举旨在实现收支平衡与健康运营，拒绝远距离配送显而易见是为了削减高额的发行运输成本，故选 [B]。

questions.stem: Compared with their American counterparts, Japanese newspapers are much more stable because they ______.
questions.analysis: 第六段通过对比指出美国报纸收入高达87%依赖广告，而日本该比例仅为35%，因此日本报纸更加稳健，即其对广告收益的依赖度明显较低，故选 [C]。

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the last paragraph about the current newspaper business?

options.label: A
options.text: Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.

options.label: B
options.text: Completeness is to blame for the failure of newspaper.

options.label: C
options.text: Foreign bureaus play a crucial role in the newspaper business.

options.label: D
options.text: Readers have lost their interest in car and film reviews.

questions.analysis: 第七段指出裁撤主要发生在报纸“least distinctive”（最不具特色）的版块，末段指出全面性不再是美德，说明报纸必须立足于其独特的特色（distinctiveness）才能生存，故选 [A]。

questions.stem: The most appropriate title for this text would be ______.

options.label: B
options.text: American Newspapers: Gone with the Wind

questions.analysis: 文章开篇设问“报纸消亡论怎么了”，接着通篇阐述美国报业面对危机通过裁员、涨价、结构重组等苦苦求存并重回微利的艰难挣扎历程，选项 [A]“美国报业：苦苦求生”最契合主旨，故选 [A]。

passages.title: Text 3 · 战后美国极简建筑风潮
paragraphs: We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with suburbs spreading and families buying new cars and larger homes. But it was also a time of significant innovation in how homes were built and how Americans lived in them.

Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living. The phrase "less is more" was coined by the German-born architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who believed that minimalism could create harmony and spaciousness even in smaller footprints.

Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance. Like other modern architects, he employed methods and materials developed for commercial buildings to design residential structures, emphasizing open floor plans and modular furniture that could serve multiple purposes.

But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of their spare furnishings. Nor was the design aesthetic popular at the time. The trend toward "less" was not entirely foreign. In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses — usually around 1,200 square feet — than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century. The "Case Study Houses" commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the "less is more" trend.

Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing. In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life — few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers — but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.
translations: 我们往往认为二战刚结束后的那几十年是一个繁荣与增长的时代，郊区不断扩张，家庭购买新车并搬入更大的住宅。但那也是在房屋建造方式以及美国人居住方式上发生重大创新的时代。
经济状况只是推动高效生活趋势的一个诱因。“少即是多”这一名言由德裔建筑师路德维希·密斯·凡·德·罗提出，他坚信极简主义即使在较小的占地面积内也能营造出和谐与宽敞感。
他认为，优雅并非源于丰裕繁复。与其他现代主义建筑师一样，他采用为商业建筑开发的方法和材料来设计住宅结构，强调开放式平面布局以及可满足多种功能需求的模块化家具。

但它们之所以受欢迎，是因为其通透的玻璃墙、开阔的视野以及简约陈设带来的高雅质感。而且这种设计美学在当时并不算完全陌生。早在20世纪30年代，弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特就开始建造更简朴、更高效的住宅（通常约1,200平方英尺），而非他在19世纪90年代和20世纪初所设计的那些占地庞大的双层豪宅。1945年至1962年间，加州《艺术与建筑》杂志委托多位杰出现代建筑师操刀的“案例研究住宅”，也是促成“少即是多”潮流的又一本土影响力来源。
美学效果来自自然景观、新型材料和直率明朗的细部设计。在拉尔夫·拉普森设计的“案例研究住宅”中，他或许未能准确预见机械革命将如何影响日常生活——几乎没有哪个美国家庭购置了直升机，尽管大多数家庭最终都配齐了烘干机——但他关于自给自足既令人向往又势在必行的信念，却得到了广泛的共鸣。

questions.stem: The postwar American housing style largely reflected the Americans' ______.
questions.analysis: 第一段末句指出居住方式发生革新，第二段明确指出“trend toward efficient living”，第三段提到开放布局与多用途家具，充分体现了对效率和实用性（efficiency and practicality）的追求，故选 [B]。

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from Paragraph 3 about the Bauhaus?

options.label: A
options.text: It was founded by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.

options.label: B
options.text: Its designing concept was affected by World War II.

options.label: C
options.text: Most American architects used to be associated with it.

options.label: D
options.text: It had a great influence upon American architecture.

questions.analysis: 密斯·凡·德·罗等包豪斯大师将商业建筑技术与极简主义思想引入美国住宅，对战后美国建筑设计理念产生了深远而持久的影响，故选 [D]。

questions.stem: Mies held that elegance of architectural design ______.

options.label: C
options.text: was not reliant on abundant decoration

questions.analysis: 第三段首句明确指出“Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance”（他认为优雅并非源于繁复堆砌），与选项 [C]“不依赖过多的装饰”完全一致，故选 [C]。

questions.stem: What is true about the apartments Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive?

options.label: B
options.text: They were built with materials popular at that time.

options.label: C
options.text: They were more spacious than neighboring buildings.

options.label: D
options.text: They shared some characteristics of abstract art.

questions.analysis: 第四段指出其通透玻璃墙、高雅简约陈设以及纯粹几何线条，展现出极简与抽象艺术的核心特质，故选 [D]。

questions.stem: What can we learn about the design of the "Case Study Houses"?

options.label: B
options.text: Natural scenes were taken into consideration.

options.label: C
options.text: Details were sacrificed for the overall effect.

questions.analysis: 最后一段首句指出“Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing”（美学效果来自景观、新材料与直率细部），即设计时充分考虑了自然景观（Natural scenes），故选 [B]。

passages.title: Text 4 · 欧元区债务危机与救赎
paragraphs: Will the European Union make it? The question would have sounded strange not long ago. Now even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a "Bermuda triangle" of debt, population decline and lower growth. As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency.

Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation. Yet the debate about how to save Europe's single currency from disintegration is stuck. It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise. Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey.

These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country's voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference. A "southern" camp headed by France wants something different: "European economic government" within an inner core of euro-zone members. Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers.

Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs. It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world's largest trading block. At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area.
It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.
translations: 欧盟能渡过难关吗？不久前，这个问题听起来还会显得很不可思议。而现在，就连该项目最忠实的拥护者也在谈论欧洲大陆正面临债务、人口负增长和经济增长乏力的“百慕大三角”。除了这些长期慢性问题，欧盟在其经济核心区——使用单一货币的16个成员国——还面临着严峻的急性危机。

市场已经对欧元区经济体（无论强弱）终有一天会通过单一货币的纪律约束走向趋同丧失了信心，因为这一机制剥夺了竞争力不足的成员国进行货币贬值这一快速应对手段。然而，关于如何拯救欧洲单一货币免于解体的争论却陷入了僵局。僵局的原因在于欧元区的主导力量法国和德国虽然一致认同欧元区内部需要加强协同，但在具体协同内容上却存在分歧。德国认为必须通过对借贷、支出和竞争力制定更严格的规则，并辅之以针对违规政府的准自动制裁，来挽救欧元。

这些制裁手段可能包括冻结流向欠发达地区及欧盟大型项目的资金，甚至暂停某一国在欧盟部长级理事会中的表决权。德国坚持认为经济协同应当涵盖欧盟俱乐部的全部27个成员国，在这些成员国中支持自由市场自由主义和紧缩经济纪律的力量占微弱多数；德国担心，如果仅限于核心圈内，支持法国式政府干预的力量将占据微弱多数。以法国为首的“南方阵营”则有不同的主张：在欧元区核心成员国内部设立“欧洲经济政府”。翻译过来，这意味着政治家插手货币政策，并通过发行共同欧洲债券为政府降低借贷成本或实现彻底的财政转移支付，建立一种从富国向穷国再分配的机制。
最后，接近法国政府的要员私下透露，欧元区成员国应当在一定程度上实现财政与社会政策的协同：例如遏制企业税率或劳动力成本方面的恶性竞争。现在唱衰欧盟还为时过早。它依然是全球最大的贸易集团。在最佳状态下，欧洲一体化项目具有非凡的自由度：围绕一个由27个富国和穷国构成的统一大市场而建，其内部边界对商品、资本和劳动力的开放程度远超任何类似贸易区。
这是一项雄心勃勃的尝试，旨在抚平全球化最锋利的棱角，让资本主义变得更加温和良善。

questions.stem: The EU is faced with so many problems that ______.

options.label: A
options.text: it has more or less lost faith in markets

options.label: B
options.text: even its supporters begin to feel concerned

options.label: C
options.text: some of its member countries plan to abandon euro

options.label: D
options.text: it intends to deny the possibility of devaluation

questions.analysis: 第一段第二句指出“Now even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a 'Bermuda triangle' of debt...”，连最坚定的支持者（cheerleaders）都在忧心忡忡地谈论危机，故选 [B]（若选项标注为 D/B，根据原文即使支持者也开始担忧，对应 [B]）。

questions.stem: The debate over the EU's single currency is stuck because the dominant powers ______.

options.label: A
options.text: are competing for the leading position

options.label: B
options.text: are busy handling their own crises

options.label: C
options.text: fail to reach an agreement on harmonisation

options.label: D
options.text: disagree on the steps towards disintegration

questions.analysis: 第二段最后两句指出僵局的原因在于德法主导国“disagree about what to harmonise”（在究竟协调什么上存在分歧），即未能在协同问题上达成一致，故选 [C]。

questions.stem: To solve the euro problem, Germany proposed that ______.

options.label: A
options.text: EU funds for poor regions be increased

options.label: C
options.text: only core members be involved in economic co-ordination

options.label: D
options.text: voting rights of the EU members be guaranteed

questions.analysis: 第二段末尾明确指出德国主张“stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions”，即施加更严格的借贷与支出规章（stricter regulations be imposed），故选 [B]。

questions.stem: The French proposal of handling the crisis implies that ______.

options.label: A
options.text: poor countries are more likely to get funds

options.label: B
options.text: strict monetary policy will be applied to poor countries

options.label: C
options.text: loans will be readily available to rich countries

options.label: D
options.text: rich countries will basically control Eurobonds

questions.analysis: 第三段末尾指出法国提议通过欧洲债券或财政转移支付实现“redistribution from richer to poorer members”，意味着贫穷成员国能够更容易获得资金救助，故选 [A]。

questions.stem: Regarding the future of the EU, the author seems to feel ______.
questions.analysis: 第四段后半部分指出“It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world's largest trading block... remarkably liberal”，末句更是赞颂其是一项雄心勃勃的伟大尝试，体现出作者对欧盟前景抱有希望（hopeful），故选 [C]。
